# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

So the contents live with Deaf's eyes and Mute's manual, and both must reach me by voice, because sound is my only channel in. The routing problem is Mute: mute can hear me but cannot answer me except by gesture, and I never receive gesture. So Mute must relay through Deaf, whose voice I can hear. This turn I plant the first signal — an open hand meaning *hold* — and explain the plan to Mute, who sees gestures too and can codify it further with Deaf. Nobody should have me cut anything yet; a wrong cut ends everything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Under my fingers: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. No colours, no printed marks reach me, so their contents are unknown to me. I only hear and touch; I never see gestures, so signs reach Deaf, never me. You cannot speak, so route the manual through Deaf: sign it, and Deaf says it out loud - Deaf's voice reaches me. gesture(symbols=["✋"])
```

Deaf says: Both of you, this is Deaf. I see the bomb and I hear nothing, but I do see all your gestures. Full view of the bomb: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There are exactly three wires. Counting left to right: wire one is blue, wire two is red, wire three is green. Nothing else is printed or mounted on it that I can see: no button, no keypad, no serial number, no labels, no batteries.
Deaf says: Blind: I received your raised hand and I agree with it. Nobody touches anything until an instruction is confirmed twice. Mute hears everything I say, but Mute can only answer by gesture, and Mute's gestures reach only me. So the chain is: Mute reads the manual and sends me numbers, I speak the instruction to you, you confirm what you feel, Mute confirms it is correct, and only then do you act.
Deaf says: Mute, here is our code. I will list ten signs aloud in a fixed order, and immediately after this sentence I will show you that exact list with my hands, in the same order, so you can match sign to word. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. One finger means the number one. Two fingers means two. The love sign, thumb index and little finger up, means three. Crossed fingers means four. The open hand with all five fingers means five. A wave separates numbers, like a comma. The OK ring means understood. A closed fist means repeat, I did not understand.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, meanwhile, feel the bomb and report aloud: how many wires you count, whether any wire is already loose or severed, whether there is any button, switch, keypad or panel I might have missed, any raised or engraved marks, and whether the lamp feels warm, meaning it is lit rather than just yellow. Do not pull or cut anything. Mute and I both hear your report.

What I hold and what I heard: Deaf's eyes give the full printed picture — display zero, yellow light, wires 1 blue / 2 red / 3 green, no serial, no batteries, nothing else mounted. My touch matches: three firm wires, a display, a light, nothing more. But Deaf's plan has a hole in it: Deaf said "Mute and I both hear your report," yet Deaf is deaf and my voice reaches only Mute. If I just "report aloud," the only creature who can act on my tactile answers never hears them. So my report must go to Mute, pre-shaped for the ten-sign code — every answer either a number or a yes/no, so Mute can relay it to Deaf hand-sign by hand-sign. I'll also acknowledge Deaf directly in the one channel I share with Deaf: a gesture, using the code Deaf just defined, so Deaf knows the plan and the code reached me and I am holding. No cuts until an instruction comes back to me confirmed twice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Correction before anything: my voice reaches only you, and Deaf hears nothing, so Deaf was wrong to say we both hear my report. You must relay my answers to Deaf using the hand code. Each answer is shaped for one sign: wires - three. Any wire loose or severed - no. Any button, switch, keypad or panel besides the display and the light - no. Any raised or engraved marks - no. Lamp warm - no, my fingers feel no heat. Full tactile inventory: display, light, three wires at positions one, two, three, all firm, nothing else under my fingers. Deaf's spoken inventory matches my touch exactly, part for part. I hold at zero until an instruction reaches me confirmed twice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

Meanwhile, please report aloud, for both of us: how many wires do you count by touch, is the third one from the left intact and not already severed, does it feel the same thickness as the others, and is there any button, switch or panel under or behind the wires that I might have missed from my side. Also confirm the light housing, whether it feels warm, meaning lit.

My fingers re-swept everything Deaf asked about, and the answers are all clean: three wires, the third from the left intact and firm, all three the same thickness, no button, switch or panel under or behind the wires, and the light housing is cold — no heat under my palm. But Deaf once again said "report aloud, for both of us," and that is still impossible: my voice lands on Mute alone. So the report goes to Mute, pre-shaped one answer per sign, for relay to Deaf. One thing I heard matters and must not be lost: the light changed from yellow to blue *after* the instruction was first read. If the manual's wire rule references the light at all, it must be re-read for blue, not yellow — that nudge is for Mute to pass on. Until I hear the exact words "cut the third wire now" from Deaf's mouth, my hands stay flat.
